symptom: MPR019 reported 39 index findings on a frontend app, all 39 on external entities (no table in this app, nothing to index). MPR017 reported 4 of 4 false findings on one solution: three attributes set by a database-connection query Map and one attribute of an external entity, each read as nothing assigns it. An import mapping setting a Boolean from JSON true had the same false positive, reproduced on a fresh project.
file: mdl/linter/rules/mpr019_unindexed_constraint.go indexableEntity; mdl/linter/rules/mpr017_fixed_guard_attribute.go guardableEntity, mappedAttributeNames, collectAttributeFacts; tests mpr017_fixed_guard_attribute_test.go, mpr019_unindexed_constraint_test.go
cause: Both rules reasoned from the model's local writes. MPR019's indexableEntity was just Persistable, which an external entity is. MPR017 counted only Change and Create members as writes, so an attribute assigned by an import mapping, a database query or an external service read as unassigned.
insight: **A rule that concludes from the ABSENCE of a write has to enumerate every writer, and the report named two of at least four.** The database query and the external entity were real; the import mapping, a far commoner writer, was not in the report and showed up only by writing the same flag through a mapping on a fresh project. The first unit test covered only the pure helper and a stub of the wiring still passed; only a test through collectAttributeFacts failed it. That test needs a file-backed catalog (an in-memory one gives each pooled connection its own empty database, #2417) and a full entity row: a missing EntityType makes Entities() fail to scan and yield nothing, so a green test over an empty fixture proves nothing. Not covered yet: export mappings and message definitions as writers, and view entities for MPR019.
